title: Transactional Apply Snapshotter with Heuristic Triggers
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a transactional "snapshot-and-apply" subsystem that captures the runtime and config-affecting state before sensitive changes, runs a lightweight heuristic simulator during staged rollouts, and exposes rollback triggers driven by cost and quality signals (batching throughput drops, KV cache hit rate regressions, token-per-response cost anomalies, latency SLO violations). The feature ties automatic rollback decisioning to a reproducible state snapshot so reconcilers can restore exact runtime state in addition to config, limiting flapping and data loss.
motivation: Recent incidents show that config rotations and automated batching/caching profile changes can unexpectedly increase per-token cost or reduce throughput. Manual rollbacks are slow and error-prone. A transactional snapshotter provides a fast, auditable way to revert both config and in-memory serving state (KV caches, active batching windows) while allowing safe automated rollbacks based on economically-relevant heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) On a staged apply, the snapshotter captures config version, in-memory KV cache manifest (keys summary), batching window metadata, and routing table; snapshots stored with TTL and audit pointer

2) Heuristic simulator runs for at least N=100 synthetic requests and estimates delta in token-cost and lat50 latency before canary traffic routes; simulator must complete within 60s for small config diffs
3) Rollback trigger can be bound to one or more signals: cost-per-1000-tokens > baseline*1.15, large drop in KV cache hit rate (>10pp), or latency P95 breach of SLO by >20% sustained over 2m
4) Automatic rollback restores runtime state from snapshot and verifies reconciliation metrics return to within 5% of pre-apply baseline within 3 minutes for test harness
5) End-to-end e2e test covering: snapshot creation, staged apply, injected cost-signal, auto-rollback, and post-rollout reconciliation passes in CI
6) Audit logs include snapshot id, trigger reason, metrics diff, recovering node ids, and PR link for the change
implementation_notes: Design: lightweight immutable snapshots stored in S3-like object store with index in config-db (snapshot metadata only). Actual KV payloads are summarized with hash + size; full payloads kept for small caches (<10MB) and truncated otherwise.
API: /apply?dry_run=true runs simulator against snapshot in a shadow lane, returning cost/latency deltas. /apply?staged=true records snapshot and applies only to 10% of traffic.
Simulator: generate synthetic traffic sampled from recent workload heatmap (seq lengths, model id, routing policy) to estimate batching and cache behavior.

Rollback: orchestrator triggers restore action that first switches routing to safe variant (pinned older model/config), then restores in-memory caches from snapshot (where available) and replays missed requests into caches where replay safe; support a 'quarantine' flag for KV keys to avoid poisoning live caches.
Data consistency: apply is transactional at control-plane level (config-db write + snapshot commit) with idempotent restore flows; careful ordering to avoid double-serve during restore.
Observability: add per-snapshot trace id, link to console UI, time-series of pre/post metrics, and cost delta scoreboard per snapshot
Rollout policy: default staged rollout = 10% -> 50% -> 100% with heuristic checks at each stage; manual override allowed by SRE or PM
test_plan: Unit tests: snapshot metadata lifecycle, snapshot TTL expiry, simulator API behavior
Integration: small-scale k8s cluster run that simulates KV cache restore and measures hit-rate before/after
Chaos tests: induce partial failures during restore and verify reconciler leaves system in consistent state and exposes clear operator actions
Load test: validate simulator run time with 10k synthetic requests and ensure stage decision latency < 60s
E2E: CI job that exercises a synthetic config change that toggles batching window and triggers automatic rollback via injected metric
progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Ticket created by Ava. Draft design sketched during sync with Runtime and Observability teams.

2025-11-07: Spike complete — prototype snapshot metadata model and simple KV payload floor. Found that full cache restores are expensive for >8MB; decide to keep payload summaries for large caches and reconstruct by replay.
2025-11-10: Simulator PoC returns stable cost deltas for seq-length distributions; need refinement for cross-model routing policies.
2025-11-13: Design review (runtime-safety) — feedback: add quarantine flag, and require explicit PM approval for enabling auto-rollback for high-impact projects. Added to policy.

2025-11-18: Implementation kicked off. Started work on snapshot metadata schema, simulator harness, and control-plane apply endpoint. Integration with console links stubbed. Assigned Liam as primary owner.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Restoring large KV caches can take long and block traffic. Mitigation: truncate payloads, reconstruct via replay, and use quarantine to serve safely while rebuilding.

Risk: False positives cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require two orthogonal signals for high-risk projects (e.g., cost+latency) and a short grace window before auto-rollback; surface manual abort option.
Risk: Snapshot storage growth. Mitigation: TTL policy, dedupe identical snapshots by content-hash, and tier older snapshots to cold storage.
Risk: Complexity in orchestration ordering leading to transient double-serving. Mitigation: atomic control-plane commits and pre-restore routing to pinned safe variant.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): internal-runtime team only; enable simulator and manual snapshot-only applies
Phase 1 (beta): selected customer projects with low traffic; enable staged applies with manual approve before auto-rollback
Phase 2 (general): auto-rollback enabled by default for non-high-impact projects with heuristics and quarantine; CLI and UI toggles available
Ops runbook: include steps for forced rollback, snapshot inspection, and how to escalate to SRE/PM
